ThefullworkflowsupportsautomatedtranslationfromGIS-baseddistrictrepresentationsto high-fidelity Modelica system models, enabling robust evaluation of alternative configura- tionsandoperationalstrategies. Two real-world district energy systems—at the University of Colorado Boulder and the University of Texas at Austin—were modeled, calibrated, and studied using the developed framework. Demonstrated benefits include improved operational efficiency, enhanced re- silience, and energy savings meeting 25% under optimized control strategies. Collectively, the project establishes an open, extensible foundation for designing next-generation grid- interactive districts and supports the widespread deployment of efficient, flexible, and re- silientcommunityenergysystems. 2 ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS This material is based upon work supported by the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy (EERE) under the Advanced Manufacturing Office,AwardNumberDE-EE0009139.
